_meta.method: complete direct literal rendering; source order preserved; no explanatory paraphrase

word_for_word: तत्र हेतुमाह नैव तस्येति
he states the reason with ‘for him there is certainly no’
कृतेन कर्मणा तस्यार्थः पुण्यं नैवास्ति
for him there is no purpose, no merit, from action performed
न चाकृतेन कश्चन कोऽपि प्रत्यवायोऽस्ति
nor is there any adverse consequence from action not performed
निरहंकारत्वेन विधिनिषेधातीतत्वात्
because through absence of ego he has transcended injunction and prohibition
तथापि तस्मात्तदेषां न प्रियं यदेतन्मनुष्या विदुः इति श्रुतेर्मोक्षे देवकृतविघ्नसंभवात्तत्परिहारार्थ कर्मभिर्देवाः सेव्या इत्याशङ्क्योक्तम्

objection: nevertheless, because Śruti says ‘that which humans know is not pleasing to these gods,’ obstacles created by gods may occur on the path to liberation, so the gods should be served through actions to remove them
सर्वभूतेषु ब्रह्मादिस्थावरान्तेषु कश्चिदप्यर्थव्यपाश्रयः आश्रय एव व्यपाश्रयः अर्थे मोक्ष आश्रयणीयोऽस्य नास्तीत्यर्थः

among all beings from Brahmā down to immovable things, he has no dependence upon any being for any purpose; ‘vyapāśraya’ means dependence; for the goal, liberation, there is nothing on which he must depend—this is the meaning
विघ्नाभावस्य श्रुत्यैवोक्तत्वात् तथाच श्रुतिः तस्य ह न देवाश्च नाभूत्या ईशते आत्मा ह्येषां स भवति इति
because absence of obstacles is itself stated by Śruti: ‘the gods are not able to cause his non-prosperity, for he becomes their Self’
देवा अपि तस्यात्मतत्त्वज्ञस्याभूत्यै ब्रह्मताप्रतिबन्धनाय नेशते न शक्नुवन्तीति श्रुतेरर्थः
the meaning of the Śruti is that even the gods cannot cause non-prosperity, cannot obstruct Brahmanhood, for the knower of the Self
देवकृतास्तु विघ्नाः सम्यग्ज्ञानोत्पत्तेः प्रागेव
obstacles created by gods occur only before right knowledge arises
यदेतद्ब्रह्म मनुष्या विदुस्तदेषां देवानां न प्रियम् इति श्रुत्या ब्रह्मज्ञानस्यैवाप्रियत्वोक्त्या तत्रैव विघ्नकर्तृत्वस्य सूचितत्वात्
for Śruti says ‘the Brahman that humans know is not pleasing to these gods’; by stating dislike specifically of Brahman-knowledge, their obstruction is indicated only at that stage
यस्मादेवंभूतस्य ज्ञानिन एव कर्मानुपयोगो नान्यस्य तस्मात्त्वं कर्म कुर्वित्याह तस्मादिति
because action is unnecessary only for a knower of this kind and not for another, therefore perform action; he says this with ‘therefore’
असक्तः फलसङ्गरहितः सन् कार्यमवश्यकर्तव्यतया विहितं नित्यनैमित्तिकं कर्म सम्यगाचर
being unattached, free from attachment to fruit, properly perform obligatory and occasional action enjoined as necessarily to be done
हि यस्मादसक्तः कर्माचरन्पुरुषः परं मोक्षं चित्तशुद्धिं ज्ञानद्वारा प्राप्नोति
for a person performing action without attachment attains the supreme, liberation, through purification of mind and knowledge
अत्र सदाचारं प्रमाणयति कर्मणैवेति
here he establishes the conduct of the good as authority with ‘by action alone’
कर्मणा एव जनकादयः संसिद्धिं प्राप्ताः
through action alone Janaka and others attained perfection
लोकसंग्रहमिति
with ‘maintenance of the world’
लोकस्य संग्रहः स्वधर्मे प्रवर्तनम्
maintenance of the world means setting people in motion in their own dharma
मया कर्मणि कृते जनः सर्वोऽपि करिष्यति
if I perform action, all people will also act
अन्यथा ज्ञानिदृष्टान्तेनाज्ञः कर्म त्यजेत्
otherwise an ignorant person may abandon action by following the example of the knower
इत्येवं लोकरक्षणमपि तावत्प्रयोजनं पश्यन्कर्म कर्तुमेवार्हसि नतु त्यक्तुमित्यर्थः
thus, seeing protection of the world itself as a purpose, you should perform action and not abandon it; this is the meaning
कर्मकरणे लोकसंग्रहो यथा स्यात्तथाह यदिति
he explains how maintenance of the world arises through performance of action with ‘whatever’
इतरः प्राकृतो जनः तत्तदेवाचरति
the other, ordinary person practices exactly what the superior person practices
स श्रेष्ठो जनः कर्मशास्त्रं निवृत्तिशास्त्रं वा यत्प्रमाणं मन्यते तदेव लोकोऽप्यनुसरति
whatever the superior person accepts as authoritative, whether scripture of action or scripture of renunciation, the world follows that very thing
अत्र चाहमेव दृष्टान्त इत्याह त्रिभिः न मे पार्थेति
here he says in three verses beginning ‘for Me, O Pārtha’ that He Himself is the example
हे पार्थ मे कर्तव्यं नास्ति
O Pārtha, there is nothing I must do
यतस्त्रिष्वपि लोकेष्वनवाप्तमप्राप्तं सदवाप्तव्यं प्राप्यं नास्ति
because in all three worlds there is nothing unattained by Me that remains to be attained
तथापि कर्मण्यहं वर्ते कर्म करोम्येवेत्यर्थः
nevertheless I remain engaged in action; I certainly act—this is the meaning
अकरणे लोकस्य नाशं दर्शयति यदीति
he shows the destruction of the world if He did not act, with ‘if’
जातु कदाचिदतन्द्रितोऽनलसः सन् यदि कर्मणि न वर्तेयं कर्म नानुतिष्ठेयम्
if ever, though tireless and not lazy, I did not engage in or perform action
तर्हि ममैव वर्त्म मार्गं मनुष्या अनुवर्तन्ते अनुवर्तेरन्नित्यर्थः
then people would follow My very path; ‘they would follow’ is the meaning
ततः किमत आह उत्सीदेयुरिति
what then? he says ‘they would perish’
उत्सीदेयुः कर्मलोपेन नश्येयुः
they would perish, be destroyed through disappearance of action
ततश्च वर्णसंकरो भवेत् तस्याप्यहमेव कर्ता स्यां भवेयम्
then mixture of varṇas would arise, and I Myself would become its cause
एवमहमेव प्रजा उपहन्यां मलिनीकुर्याम्
thus I Myself would harm, corrupt, the creatures
तस्मादात्मविदापि लोकसंग्रहार्थं तत्कृपया कर्म कार्यमेवेत्युपसंहरति सक्ता इति
therefore, even by a knower of the Self, action must be performed for maintenance of the world out of compassion for it; he concludes with ‘attached’
कर्मणि सक्ता अभिनिविष्टाः सन्तोऽज्ञाः यथा कर्म कुर्वन्ति
just as ignorant people, attached and deeply fixed in action, perform action
तथैव असक्तः सन् विद्वानपि कुर्यात् लोकसंग्रहं कर्तुमिच्छुः
so also the knower should act without attachment, desiring to maintain the world
ननु कृपया तत्त्वज्ञानमेवोपदेष्टुं युक्तं नेत्याह नेति
objection: out of compassion, should one not teach knowledge of reality itself? he says ‘no’
अज्ञानामतएव कर्मसङ्गिनां कर्मासक्तानामकर्तात्मोपदेशेन बुद्धेर्भेदमन्यथात्वं न जनयेत्
one should not produce disruption, alteration, in the understanding of ignorant persons who for that very reason are attached to action, by teaching them that the Self is a non-doer
कर्मणः सकाशाद्बुद्धिचालनं न कुर्यात् अपि तु जोषयेत् सेवयेत् जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः
one should not move their understanding away from action, but should make them delight in, serve, action; the root juṣ has the senses of delight and service
अज्ञान्कर्माणि कारयेत्
one should cause the ignorant to perform actions
कथम् युक्तोऽवहितो भूत्वा स्वयं च समाचरन्
how? being disciplined and attentive, while oneself practicing properly
बुद्धिचालने कृते सति कर्मसु श्रद्धानिवृत्तेर्ज्ञानस्य चानुत्पत्तेस्तेषामुभयभ्रंशः स्यादिति भावः
if their understanding were disturbed, their faith in action would cease and knowledge would not arise, so they would lose both; this is the intention
ननु विदुषापि चेत्कर्म कर्तव्यं तर्हि विद्वदविदुषोः को विशेष इत्याशङ्क्योभयोर्विशेषं दर्शयति प्रकृतेरिति द्वाभ्याम्

objection: if even the knower must perform action, what difference is there between knower and ignorant person? anticipating this, he shows the distinction between the two in two verses beginning ‘of prakṛti’
प्रकृतेर्गुणैः प्रकृतिकार्यैरिन्द्रियैः सर्वप्रकारेण क्रियमाणानि यानि कर्माणि
actions that are in every way performed by the guṇas of prakṛti, that is, by the senses which are products of prakṛti
तान्यहमेव कर्ता करोमीति मन्यते
he thinks ‘I myself am the doer; I perform them’
तत्र हेतुः अहंकारेणेन्द्रियादिष्वात्माध्यासेन विमूढ आत्मा बुद्धिर्यस्य सः
the reason: his inner being, his understanding, is deluded by ego, by superimposition of the Self upon the senses and the like
विद्वांस्तु तथा न मन्यत इत्याह तत्त्वविदिति
the knower does not think so; he says this with ‘the knower of truth’
नाहं गुणात्मक इति गुणेभ्य आत्मनो विभागः
‘I am not constituted of the guṇas’: this is separation of the Self from the guṇas
न मे कर्माणीति कर्मभ्योऽप्यात्मनो विभागः
‘actions are not mine’: this is separation of the Self from actions
तयोर्गुणकर्मविभागयोर्यस्तत्त्वं वेत्ति स तु न सज्जते कर्तृत्वाभिनिवेशं न करोति
one who knows the truth of these divisions between guṇas and action does not become attached and does not insist upon doership
तत्र हेतुः गुणा इन्द्रियाणि गुणेषु विषयेषु वर्तन्ते नाहमिति मत्वा
the reason: thinking ‘the guṇas, the senses, operate among the guṇas, the objects; not I’
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदित्युक्तमुपसंहरति प्रकृतेरिति
he concludes what was said, ‘one should not disturb their understanding,’ with ‘of prakṛti’
यैः प्रकृतेर्गुणैः सत्त्वादिभिः संमूढाः सन्तो गुणेष्विन्द्रियेषु तत्कर्मसु च सज्जन्ते वयं कुर्म इति
those deluded by the guṇas of prakṛti, sattva and the others, become attached to the guṇas, the senses, and their actions, thinking ‘we act’
तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दमतीन् कृत्स्नवित्सर्वज्ञो न विचालयेत्
the knower of the whole, the fully knowing person, should not unsettle those who do not know the whole and are of dull understanding
तदेवं तत्त्वविदापि कर्म कर्तव्यं त्वं तु नाद्यापि तत्त्ववित् अतः कर्मैव कुर्वित्याह मयीति
thus action must be performed even by a knower of truth; but you are not yet a knower of truth, therefore perform action; he says this with ‘in Me’
सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य समर्प्य
renouncing, offering, all actions in Me
अध्यात्मचेतसा अन्तर्याम्यधीनोऽहं करोमीति दृष्ट्या
with a mind directed to the Self, with the view ‘I act under the control of the Inner Ruler’
निराशीर्निष्कामोऽतएव मत्फलसाधनं मदर्थमिदं कर्मेत्येवं ममताशून्यश्च भूत्वा
being without expectation, desireless, and therefore free from possessiveness with the thought ‘this action is for Me and is a means to My result’
विगतज्वरस्त्यक्तशोकश्च भूत्वा युध्यस्व
becoming free from fever, having abandoned grief, fight
